hoogle:src/General/Web.hs:178:Cross-Site.vuln: Cross-Site Scripting (HTML response body from text)
hoogle:src/General/Web.hs:178:Cross-Site.label: ambiguous
hoogle:src/General/Web.hs:178:Cross-Site.reason: The text of an exception raised while answering the request is written as a 500 body with no content type. Query parsing returns errors as values rather than throwing, so the text is normally an internal error, but an exception that quoted the request would be reflected without a declared type; a browser may sniff it. Not shown either way.

hoogle:src/General/Web.hs:180:path-trave.vuln: Path Traversal (file served from a request-chosen path)
hoogle:src/General/Web.hs:180:path-trave.label: FP
hoogle:src/General/Web.hs:180:path-trave.reason: responseFile serves joinPath (htmlDir : segments), but every request path is parsed by readInput, which returns Nothing (a 400) for any segment that is "..", "." or contains a separator (badSegment), so no traversal reaches the file operation. The engine does not read a validation inside a Maybe-returning constructor.

servant:servant-server/src/Servant/Serve.label: FP
servant:servant-server/src/Servant/Serve.reason: responseLBS of a ServerError: the flow is the Accept header into acceptCheck, whose RESULT (a Delayed carrying err406) the engine treats as tainted because a call with a tainted argument returns tainted; err406's body is a fixed string and the header is never echoed.

servant:servant-auth/servant-auth-server.vuln: Session cookie without HttpOnly or Secure
servant:servant-auth/servant-auth-server.label: FP
servant:servant-auth/servant-auth-server.reason: servant-auth-server's cookie builders: the session cookie gets HttpOnly True in applySessionCookieSettings and Secure from the settings (default Secure); the XSRF token cookie is HttpOnly False by design, since the client script must read it to send the header. postgrest:src/library/PostgREST/App.hs:2.vuln: Cross-Site Scripting (HTML response body from text)
postgrest:src/library/PostgREST/App.hs:2.label: FP
postgrest:src/library/PostgREST/App.hs:2.reason: toWaiResponse hands on the PgrstResponse the handler built: the content type is in `hdrs`, negotiated from the request's Accept against the schema's media types, and the body is what the database returned. The rule reads a content type only from a literal header list, never from a parameter's field, and keeps an opaque header list as HTML. No HTML is rendered from request text here.

postgrest:src/library/PostgREST/App.hs:2.vuln: Request body read without a size limit

yesod:yesod-static/Yesod/EmbeddedStatic/.vuln: Cross-Site Scripting (HTML response body from text)
yesod:yesod-static/Yesod/EmbeddedStatic/.label: FP
yesod:yesod-static/Yesod/EmbeddedStatic/.reason: The development-mode static server: `f (drop 1 (pathInfo r))` looks a file up by path and returns its content with its own mime type, and `responseLBS status200 [("Content-Type", mime), ("ETag", hash)] ct` serves that file. The body is a file of the project's static directory, not request text rendered into a page; the engine taints the result of an unknown function-typed parameter applied to the path. Not fixed: the lookup is a parameter, and its contract (a file keyed by path) is not visible.

yesod:yesod/Yesod/Default/Util.hs:52:pat.label: FP
yesod:yesod/Yesod/Default/Util.hs:52:pat.reason: `addStaticContentExternal minify hash staticDir toRoute ext' _ content` is a helper that implementations of `addStaticContent` call with a literal extension ("js", "css") and the content to store; the file name is the content's hash plus that extension under `staticDir </> "tmp"`. Its parameters are the caller's, not route pieces: the function returns `HandlerFor`, which the model took as a route handler. Fixed in round 5: only a dispatch-named handler (getFooR, postFooR, handleFooR) takes request input from its parameters.

yesod:yesod-auth/Yesod/Auth/Email.hs:959.vuln: Password hashed with a fast general-purpose hash
yesod:yesod-auth/Yesod/Auth/Email.hs:959.label: FP
yesod:yesod-auth/Yesod/Auth/Email.hs:959.reason: `saltPass'` is the legacy MD5 verifier kept for passwords hashed before PasswordStore: `isValidPass ct salted = PS.verifyPassword .. || isValidPass' ct salted`, and `isValidPass'` only compares `salted == saltPass' salt clear`; `saltPass` (the one that stores) uses `PS.makePassword`. The migration shape the rule recognises, except that the KDF is `Yesod.Auth.Util.PasswordStore`, a vendored copy of the password-store package under another module name, and the KDF sits one hop ABOVE the comparing function. Not fixed this round: recognising a vendored KDF module needs its construction read (STRef loop, not `iterate`).

yesod:yesod-core/src/Yesod/Core/Class/Ye.vuln: Session cookie without HttpOnly or Secure
yesod:yesod-core/src/Yesod/Core/Class/Ye.label: ambiguous
yesod:yesod-core/src/Yesod/Core/Class/Ye.reason: The default client-session backend's cookie: HttpOnly is set, Secure is not, and Yesod documents `sslOnlySessions` / `sslOnlyMiddleware` as the way to add it. A framework default that is right for local development over HTTP and wrong for a deployment that forgets the wrapper; the finding is accurate about the cookie and cannot know the deployment.

yesod:yesod-core/src/Yesod/Core/Handler..vuln: Session cookie without HttpOnly or Secure
yesod:yesod-core/src/Yesod/Core/Handler..label: ambiguous
yesod:yesod-core/src/Yesod/Core/Handler..reason: `setCsrfCookie` writes the XSRF-TOKEN double-submit cookie with `defaultSetCookie`: readable by the page's script by design (the rule already does not ask for HttpOnly), and without Secure, which `setCsrfCookieWithCookie` lets the application add. A CSRF token is not a session credential, so the stake of its exposure in transit is lower than the rule's title says; recorded as ambiguous rather than FP because the attribute is genuinely absent.

yesod:yesod-core/src/Yesod/Core/TypeCach.vuln: Partial function applied to caller-supplied text
yesod:yesod-core/src/Yesod/Core/TypeCach.label: FP
yesod:yesod-core/src/Yesod/Core/TypeCach.reason: `fromJust` here is a where-bound definition (`fromJust = error ..`, evaluated only for its type under `typeOf`), not Data.Maybe.fromJust; the module defines the name. Fixed in round 5: a partial name the module defines itself is that definition.

keter:src/Keter/Proxy.hs:203:Cross-Site.vuln: Cross-Site Scripting (HTML response body from text)
keter:src/Keter/Proxy.hs:203:Cross-Site.label: FP
keter:src/Keter/Proxy.hs:203:Cross-Site.reason: The 404 body is `psUnknownHost host`, a function chosen when the settings are read: the default `defaultUnknownHostBody` escapes the host (`escapeHtml`, blaze-builder's `fromHtmlEscapedByteString`), and a configured response file ignores it (`const`). The header also escapes it. The engine taints the result of a function-valued record field applied to the host. Not fixed: a configuration-selected function value.

keter:src/Keter/Rewrite.hs:135:Server-Si.label: FP
keter:src/Keter/Rewrite.hs:135:Server-Si.reason: `simpleReverseProxy` is a reverse proxy: `mkRequest` takes host, port and scheme from the ReverseProxyConfig (`reversedHost rpConfig`, `reversedPort rpConfig`, `reversedUseSSL rpConfig`) and only the path, query string, headers and body from the client's request. The destination is the operator's; the request content is what a proxy forwards. Not fixed this round: the fixed-host judgement reads a literal host, not a configuration field.

keter:src/Keter/Cli.hs:93:Whole input re.vuln: Whole input read into memory without a size limit
keter:src/Keter/Cli.hs:93:Whole input re.label: FP
keter:src/Keter/Cli.hs:93:Whole input re.reason: `recv conn 1024` in `talk`, which decodes each message, answers it and recurses with the socket alone (`when isLoop $ talk conn`): one chunk of at most 1024 bytes is held at a time. The loop rule asked only for a recursive call. Fixed in round 5: the recursive call must carry a value built from the read.
